core_idea: Instead of a fixed query engine, a pipeline of LLM agents analyses the workload and hardware, designs storage and indexes, plans the query, generates per-query C++ executables, and iteratively refines them from runtime feedback.

family_reason: The gain comes from feeding fuzzing, static-analysis and runtime-monitoring findings (CWE-classified error reports) back to GPT-4 for patching; the named 'agents' are vaguely specified add-ons around that loop.

gain_note: Table III (All Agents vs LLM Only); single-agent columns are ablations. No counts of programs, tasks or vulnerabilities are ever given, so VRR cannot be traced to denominators; agents are said to be 'powered by specialized machine learning models' that are never identified.
core_idea: GPT-4 generates FreeRTOS firmware, which is fuzzed, statically analyzed and runtime-monitored in QEMU; CWE-classified findings are fed back for iterative LLM patching with threat-detection, performance and compliance agents.

family_reason: A profile-diagnose-optimize-verify loop driven by profiler measurements and a noise-floor acceptance gate does the work; the knowledge base is supporting context.
scope_reason: Optimizes an existing human-written production serving stack (Triton C++, Python preprocessor, PyTorch model, GPU kernels) rather than LLM-generated programs from a specification; the LLM-edited code's efficiency is the outcome.

Table 3: preprocessor 940 to about 1.5k RPS/pod. All results are in-house case studies; the LLM is never named.
core_idea: An always-on agent loop that profiles one serving-stack layer at a time, diagnoses bottlenecks against a layer knowledge base, applies a code or configuration change, and accepts it only if a full-stack load test shows gains above measurement noise.

family_reason: Gains come from LoRA SFT of QwQ-32B on a curated dataset selected for short reasoning traces and high speedup.

On Level 1 the strongest baseline DeepSeek-R1-0528 CUDA (18.0) slightly beats KernelCoder (17.0). The quoted sentence states the gain only against the base model; no sentence gives both numbers.
core_idea: Synthesize CUDA kernels with reasoning traces via Kevin-32B, keep correct ones where the shortest trace also has the top speedup (plus very fast kernels and a balanced single-operator share), and LoRA-fine-tune QwQ-32B on the 4,892 examples.

family_reason: Gains come from RL training where an agentic grader's quality ranks redistribute GRPO advantages among test-passing rollouts.
scope_reason: Outcome includes implementation quality (precision, minimality, side effects, consistency) of LLM-generated repository patches.

Gagar achieves a mean quality score of 4.03

core_idea: During code-agent RL, an SFT-trained agentic grader jointly inspects all rollouts of a task, ranks test-passing ones on five quality criteria, and a sum-preserving rescaling shifts positive advantage toward higher-quality passes.

family_reason: Per-function LLM rewrites are driven by compile gates (idiomaticity as hard errors) and runtime trace-divergence feedback.
scope_reason: Outcome is memory safety/idiomaticity of LLM-rewritten Rust in a C-to-Rust migration of an existing project, i.e. LLM editing of human-written code rather than generation from a specification.

core_idea: Start from a lossless c2rust translation and replace functions leaf-first with LLM reimplementations that must pass a compile gate enforcing five idiomatic-Rust criteria and a runtime equivalence gate with trace-divergence feedback.

family_reason: The novel component is a PPO-trained lightweight policy LLM that proposes semantic optimization actions; ablations show removing the learned policy causes the largest drop, while a general LLM implements each step.

core_idea: Macro Thinking: an RL-trained small LLM picks step-wise semantic optimization actions (tiling, fusion, pipelining, reordering plus code region); Micro Coding: a general LLM implements each step with in-context examples.

family_reason: Nsight Compute profiling metrics and compile/runtime errors are fed back to the LLM over iterative optimization rounds.

LLM E2E achieves higher success rate to

generated by BetterV have 46.52% fewer nodes than the

core_idea: Instruct-tune a code LLM on Verilog (Verilog-C alignment, autocompletion, augmentation) and guide decoding with a small generative discriminator trained to prefer Verilog with a desired EDA attribute (fewer nodes, faster SAT).

family_reason: An LLM mutation loop driven by compile/correctness gates, multi-fidelity latency measurement and Nsight Compute profiling feedback does most of the work.
scope_reason: Outcome is runtime speedup of LLM-generated/edited Triton GPU kernels.

core_idea: Budget-aware coarse-to-fine LLM mutation search over Triton kernels with expert-hint seeds, policy/correctness gates, rung-based multi-fidelity promotion and profiler-conditioned prompts.

family_reason: The LLM emits a JSON circuit IR that the compiler type-checks and statically analyzes, feeding errors back for up to 3 refinement rounds; deterministic CIRCT lowering/optimization follows.

core_idea: Python DSL fixes module interfaces/hierarchy, the LLM generates a JSON circuit IR whose widths are inferred and statically checked with feedback, then lowered to CIRCT and optimized into Verilog.

family_reason: TicTacSkill is a skill document of timing-closure SOPs given to the coding agent before solving; it changes only the guidance in context.

core_idea: An agent skill encoding timing-closure standard operating procedures (critical-path localization, datapath/pipeline/control checks, evidence-driven search, pre/post-PnR mismatch handling) derived from failure analysis of agent trajectories.

family_reason: The pipeline relies on build-error fix and test-alignment recovery steps driven by compiler and black-box test feedback.

core_idea: LLM pipeline in the Fission serverless platform that translates Python functions to Go with documentation, build-fix and test-alignment recovery steps, deploying the translation only if black-box tests pass.

family_reason: Candidates are generated, evaluated with simulation/Yosys/ABC/GEMM tools, scored and promoted across versions; skill evolution is secondary.

core_idea: Versioned major/minor Verilog candidate search with multi-tool executable feedback (iverilog, Yosys, ABC, GEMM evaluator), configurable multi-objective promotion, and validation-gated cross-session skill evolution.

family_reason: Iterative generate-verify-profile loop: compilation/function errors and fastest-kernel performance are fed back into refined prompts up to depth D.

core_idea: Feature Search and Reinforcement: generate N CUDA kernels, filter by compilation verifier and function validator, select the fastest via GPU profiling, and refine the prompt with errors or performance hints for D rounds.

family_reason: A Planner, parallel CUDA Coders, a Synthesizer, an NCU Profiler and a web Researcher coordinate in Houmao to drive the optimization.

core_idea: Team-based AutoResearch-style multi-agent workflow (Planner, parallel CUDA Coders, Synthesizer, NCU Profiler, web Researcher) with CUDA skills, anti-hacking rules and human search correction to optimize GPU kernels.

family_reason: A LoRA fine-tuned LLM generates the budget-constrained TPU Verilog header, with RAG retrieving dependent modules.

baseline_name: Manual optimization by an expert hardware designer
gain_quote: reduction in area and power of 92% and 96% from the manual
gain_note: Headline appears only in abstract/conclusion; Fig 9 plots PPA for 4 DNN workloads with no per-workload numbers in text; no no-technique LLM baseline. Quote holds the technique's reported reductions (92% area, 96% power), not paired values.
core_idea: Framework that turns user specs into templated prompts for a LoRA fine-tuned LLM generating systolic-array TPU Verilog headers, retrieves dependent modules via RAG, and validates with Yosys/OpenROAD.

family_reason: The gains come from SFT on a curated Triton dataset followed by GRPO reinforcement learning; no inference-time loop is used.

Efficiency is mixed against the strongest baselines elsewhere: TritonBench-T fast1 17.04 vs DeepSeek-R1-0120 22.89; KernelBench L1 fast1 10.0 vs Claude-4-Sonnet 11.0; L2 fast1 17.0 vs DeepSeek-R1-0528 28.0. The reward is correctness plus a Triton-syntax rule only; the authors state there is no performance-guided training, so speed gains are a by-product.
core_idea: Fine-tune an 8B reasoning code model on distilled and compiled PyTorch-to-Triton data, then apply GRPO with a reward that requires both passing tests and genuine Triton code.

family_reason: An agent iteratively edits a training script, runs it and keeps candidates by measured results, with a genetic (and self-modifiable) controller choosing parents.
scope_reason: The objective is validation bits-per-byte of the trained language model; peak VRAM of the edited training script is a secondary by-product, not the NF quality of code.

core_idea: Replace AutoResearch's keep-or-discard hill climbing with a population of elite research states expanded by LLM mutation and crossover, where the agent may also edit the genetic controller itself.

WAMJET is faster than the no-harness agent in all 12 agent x WAM entries, but each is a single run and the authors defer matched-budget comparisons to future work.
core_idea: Give a coding agent reusable optimization guidance, profiling/timing tools, output and state checks and paired task evaluation so it iteratively accelerates world-action-model inference code.

core_idea: Learn PPA optimization rules automatically by contrasting functionally equivalent LLM rewrites (Explore-Evaluate-Induce), then retrieve, adapt and apply them inside a rule-guided beam search over RTL rewrites.

family_reason: A long-horizon LLM agent proposes assembly edits that are rebuilt, verified for equivalence and timed, with only verified speedups committed.

core_idea: Recover reassemblable AMDGCN assembly from a compiled GPU code object, let a long-horizon LLM agent edit profiled hot windows, rebuild ABI-preserving objects and commit only differentially verified, faster candidates.

family_reason: The pipeline splits MATLAB-to-HLS conversion across specialized agents with standardized interfaces, each validated by deterministic tools.

core_idea: Convert MATLAB algorithms to HLS C++ with a chain of rule-guided agents (modularization, test data, flattening, streaming optimization from a pattern library, algorithm-hardware co-design, translation, DSE refinement, integration) validated by simulation.

family_reason: The method fine-tunes code models with DPO (or SFT) on self-generated preference pairs labeled by correctness and runtime.

core_idea: Sample many solutions from the base model, label them by tests and measured runtime, and fine-tune with DPO on quick-vs-slow and passed-vs-failed pairs re-drawn every epoch.

family_reason: An agent loop edits RTL, synthesizes it and keeps only FoM-lowering candidates; the adaptive effort policy schedules reasoning depth within that loop.

family_reason: A hardware-CWE knowledge graph built offline is explored by clue-guided retrieval and the retrieved mitigations and examples are put in the generation prompt, which carries the gain.
scope_reason: Outcome is the security of LLM-generated Verilog (functionally correct samples that pass MITRE-derived security tests).

core_idea: Build a Hardware-CWE knowledge graph with instance-adaptive CoT extraction verified by a fine-tuned BERT classifier, then retrieve evidence subgraphs by LLM-guided clue exploration and prompt the LLM with mitigations and examples to generate secure Verilog.

Online function notebook is built from unit-test failures during evaluation, possible leakage.
core_idea: Retrieval-augmented secure generation that adds contrastive error notes from a Security Error Notebook (past CodeQL/Semgrep failures with fixes) and a Function Error Notebook (past unit-test failures) to hierarchical security knowledge, with notebooks updated online.

family_reason: An autonomous coding agent iterates edit-compile-test-profile against a correctness and throughput scoring function over a 7-day lineage; execution feedback drives the gains.

scope_reason: Outcome is the throughput of LLM-generated GEMM code.

family_reason: Empirical profiling over an input-size schedule and log-log complexity fitting route targeted patches back to the coder or planner; the profiling loop does the work.
scope_reason: Targets efficiency (TLE/MLE, asymptotic complexity) of LLM-generated competitive-programming code.

SwiftSolve improves run-level success (73.1% vs.
52.6%)
gain_note: Abstract. Success mixes correctness and resource limits; EFF@k and complexity-fit accuracy are defined but not reported. Per-dataset Claude numbers (62.5% BigO, 46.7% Codeforces) do not reproduce 52.6% overall. Runtime 12.4 s vs 6.8 s.
core_idea: Planner, static pruner, coder, profiler and complexity-analyst agents that profile C++ candidates over growing input sizes, fit log-log runtime slopes to a complexity class, and dispatch patches or replans until the code is efficient.

family_reason: A coordinator spawns per-sub-kernel optimizer agents and then N parallel exploration agents; scaling the number of agents is the studied lever.

Table II gives 4.31x, 4.92x, 7.07x, 6.53x under columns 1->2, 2->4, 4->8, 8->10, so 7.07x is the N=8 value and N=10 is 6.53x; the intro states 8.27x and streamcluster >20x while results say streamcluster ~5-6x. Baseline definition differs across suites (bounded exhaustive pragma search vs reference implementations); no comparison to SOTA DSE.
core_idea: Agent factory: per-sub-kernel optimizer agents generate pragma/code variants, an agent-formulated ILP picks top-N combinations under an area budget, then N exploration agents apply cross-function optimizations.

family_reason: A compile-validate-profile loop feeds filtered profiler bottleneck metrics and a history buffer back to the LLM; hardware context plus profiler feedback drive the gain.
scope_reason: Outcome is speedup and L2 hit rate of LLM-edited GPU kernels.
gain_metric: average end-to-end kernel speedup over unswizzled kernels, 10 GPU kernels on MI300X
gain_quote: Across the 10 kernels, SwizzlePerf achieves an average speedup of 1.29× and up to a 2.06× on the

core_idea: Hardware-aware optimization loop that gives the LLM parsed profiler bottleneck metrics, GPU/XCD/cache attributes and the block-scheduling policy, plus a history of past attempts, to generate workgroup swizzling patterns that raise L2 locality.

family_reason: A coding agent iterates over rounds using hidden-testbench, simulation cycle and post-route timing feedback, first at HLS level then on the generated RTL.
scope_reason: Outcome is execution time and resources of agent-generated hardware designs (HLS C++ and Verilog).
gain_metric: geometric-mean speedup over Direct RTL Design (cycles x clock period)
gain_quote: 2.31× geometric-mean speedup over Direct RTL Design, while subsequent RTL refinement increases the speedup to 2.62×.
gain_note: Section 5.4 / Table 3. Both relative to Direct RTL Design (1.00x); HLS-only uses n=15 pairs, AHRR n=13. Each experiment runs once.
core_idea: AHRR: the agent first writes and optimizes HLS C++ that Vitis HLS turns into RTL, then refines the generated Verilog directly, with per-round evaluation feedback.

family_reason: Dedicated LLM agents (SCE Manager, Strategy Translator, Kernel Revisor, Roofline Prophet) split strategy-level evolution from strategy-to-kernel translation; this decomposition is the core contribution.
scope_reason: Outcome is runtime speedup of LLM-generated CUDA kernels (efficiency).
gain_metric: average speedup over PyTorch on KernelBench level-1 (100 kernels, DeepSeek-R1)
gain_quote: Overall, an average speedup of 3.09× is achieved.
gain_note: Section 5.2. AI CUDA Engineer (the stronger agentic baseline) is shown only per kernel in Fig. 5 on a log scale with no aggregate number, so the numeric baseline is PyTorch. No correctness rate reported; single run on the main benchmark; ablations (3 repeats) on 4 kernels: -44.2% latency (roofline), -54.1% (strategy pool).
core_idea: Strategy-coordinated evolutionary multi-agent framework that crosses optimization strategies (not code), translates them to CUDA kernels, guides prompts by roofline position, and seeds the population via RAG over a historical strategy pool.

family_reason: Simulator error feedback (VeriRectify) and PPA-constraint feedback from logic synthesis drive iterative LLM regeneration.
scope_reason: NF outcome is hardware PPA (clock/power/area) of LLM-generated Verilog, mapped to efficiency.
gain_metric: clock period (ps) of adder_32bit after PPA-constrained optimization (GPT-4)
gain_quote: adder 32bit, can be synthesized with a 500ps clock as shown
gain_note: Technique value 180 ps from line 1024-1025 ('the adder 32bit operates at an improved 180ps clock') and Table VII; baseline 500 ps from Table VI and Fig. 3. PPA optimization shown on only 4 designs (Table VII) with no systematic comparison; power rises from 14.7 to 587.31 uW and area from 213.2 to 1005.67 um2 for this design. Headline numbers in the abstract are correctness, not PPA.
core_idea: Two-stage Verilog generation: simulator-error feedback loop for syntax/functional correctness, then synthesis PPA check with PPA-aware 4-shot in-context prompt fed back until constraints are met.

family_reason: An LLM evolutionary loop (select parent, design experiments, write kernel) driven only by end-to-end timing feedback from the competition platform.
scope_reason: Outcome is execution time of LLM-generated HIP kernels (efficiency).
gain_metric: geometric average execution time (microseconds) over 18 matrix sizes, AMD MI300 FP8 GEMM
gain_note: Table 1 is garbled: PyTorch reference '≈ 850' is at line 414, Naive HIP '≈ 5000' and this work '≈ 450' at lines 428-429. Values are approximate. The human 1st-place entry (105 us) beats the technique; it is a leaderboard reference rather than a method baseline. Single task, single run.
core_idea: LLM-driven evolutionary kernel optimization with three stages: evolutionary selector picks base/reference kernels, experiment designer proposes and rates experiments, kernel writer implements them; timing from an external benchmark is the only feedback.

family_reason: A pipeline of separate agents (pseudocode generation, solution generation, test generation) plus execution verification produces the code.
scope_reason: Headline outcome is correctness and algorithmic faithfulness; readability (Clarity) is only one LLM-judge rubric dimension.
gain_metric: Clarity score 1-5 (GPT-5 rubric judge) on Pseudo2CodeQA (300 tasks)
gain_note: Table II, Clarity column: Direct 4.33 and Agentic Pipeline 4.77 appear on consecutive lines (636-637) because of table extraction. Judge scores have no validation statistics; Direct scores are identical to the Gemini 2.5 Pro row. Human evaluation covers only the agentic pipeline (no baseline).
core_idea: Agentic code generation that first produces structured pseudocode, then code constrained to it, then LLM-generated tests and execution-based verification.

family_reason: Search-Space Decision, Strategy Planning and Optimization agents plan implementation space and direction; the planning ablation causes the largest speedup loss.
scope_reason: Outcome is speedup of LLM-generated GPU kernels over PyTorch (efficiency).
gain_metric: fast1 (% of KernelBench L1-3 tasks faster than PyTorch) at budget B=18, averaged over base LLMs
gain_quote:
reaches 92.4% fast0 and 60.4% fast1 , exceeding KernelBench
(85.2%/ 29.6%) and CUDAForge (85.6%/ 44.8%)
gain_note: Results section RQ1 (Fig. 3), lines 405-406. CUDA-L1 (training-based) reported per level in Table 2 only. Single run per configuration; budget points from the same trajectories.
core_idea: Hierarchical planning for GPU kernel optimization: contract-augmented task spec, agent selects implementation space (custom CUDA, CUDA libraries, PyTorch ops) and optimization direction, then refines with NCU profiling feedback.

family_reason: Monte Carlo tree search over LLM tokens with compile/function/ADP reward replaces greedy decoding.
scope_reason: Outcome is area-delay product of LLM-generated Verilog (hardware efficiency).
gain_metric: area-delay product (x10^3) of 16-bit adder from Yosys synthesis
gain_note: Table 3 (garbled): lines 829-830 hold BS and MCTS ADP for 16- and 32-bit adders (31.8% and 19.6% improvement). Baselines produce functional code for few modules, so ADP compares only 4 modules; average 5.69% over VeriGen and 14.27% over beam search.
core_idea: MCTS-guided decoding of a Verilog LLM with reward from compilation, functional simulation and synthesized area-delay product, pruning comment tokens and reusing generated submodules for large designs.

family_reason: AlphaEvolve evolutionary search scored by real TPU latency and XProf trace feedback, gated by correctness and security checks.
scope_reason: Outcome is latency of LLM-edited FHE kernels (efficiency).
gain_metric: TFHE bootstrap latency (ms) on TPUv5e
baseline_name: Jaxite human-engineered state of the art
gain_note: Table I, Post-AlphaEvolve bootstrap row (2.5x). CKKS-Rot text gives 4874->3754 us while Table I gives 4854->3714 us (minor inconsistency, not the headline). Single run, no variance; underlying LLMs not named; best program merged after human review.
core_idea: Adapt AlphaEvolve to optimize JAX/Pallas FHE kernels on TPUs using hardware-in-the-loop latency as fitness, profiler traces as feedback, and correctness/security checks to reject candidates.

family_reason: Coder, Verifier, Profiler and Conductor agents form the loop; the Conductor interprets profiling data to guide the Coder.
scope_reason: Outcome is speedup of LLM-generated kernels over Torch (efficiency).
gain_metric: average speedup over Torch on KernelBench, GPU (Triton), DeepSeek-R1
baseline_name: N-PRAGMA (same multi-agent system without profiling feedback)
gain_note: Table I (garbled): lines 479-481 give N-PRAGMA speedup 1.28, its Fast1 32.2, PRAGMA speedup 2.30. Caesar 0.51. Number of KernelBench tasks not stated; single model, single run. Text says 1.90x over N-PRAGMA on GPU while 2.30/1.28 is about 1.80.
core_idea: Profile-guided multi-agent kernel generation where a Conductor agent maps NCU/perf metrics to optimization hints for a Coder agent, retaining the historically best kernel and its profile.

family_reason: Although framed as four agents, the work is done by compile/test error feedback and a register-usage (liveness analysis) plus measured-speedup feedback loop with performance-based selection.
scope_reason: Outcome is the runtime performance of LLM-translated RVV intrinsic code measured on hardware.
gain_metric: speedup vs native expert-written RVV intrinsics (Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Table III)
baseline_name: IntrinTrans translated-only (no register-usage-and-speedup feedback), same model
gain_quote:
compared to before the introduction
of register-usage-and-speedup feedback, the performance of
these tasks improved by an average of 9.19% to 34.87%.
gain_note: Table III lists translated vs optimized speedup per model (Claude-Sonnet-4.5 1.01 -> 1.28, +25.99%); table values sit on separate lines so the quote is the sentence stating the gain range across models. External rule-based baseline Neon2RVV is 0.63 (weaker). Text says 50 tasks but pass rates (97.1%, 94.1%, 88.2%) imply a denominator of 34. Single run at temperature 0.2, one optimization iteration.
core_idea: An FSM-orchestrated LLM agent translates Arm Neon intrinsics to RVV intrinsics, repairs them with compile and test feedback, then optimizes them using LLVM liveness-analysis register-pressure feedback and on-device speedup measurements, keeping the fastest correct variant.

family_reason: The autonomous system works by having the coding agent invoke a library of Agent Skills distilled from documented optimization and debugging experience, with numerical gates as checks.
scope_reason: Outcome is the runtime performance (TTFT, decode throughput) of NPU deployment code written by an LLM coding agent.
gain_metric: decode speedup over hand-optimized IRON BF16 Llama-3.2-1B (x)
gain_quote:
The resulting implementation achieves a speedup of
2.2× on prefill and 4.0× on decode over the hand-optimized
baseline
gain_note: Headline speedups come from the human-guided, agent-assisted Llama-3.2-1B reference deployment (stage one), not from the autonomous skill system; baseline value is the normalized 1.0x. Autonomous deployments (Table II) only report eta_scale relative to that reference (0.24-1.07 prefill, 0.28-1.27 decode) with no agent-without-skills baseline. Single run per model.
core_idea: Distill a documented human-guided NPU deployment trajectory into an eight-phase Agent Skill chain with numerical correctness gates, optimization and debug skills, and an independent evaluator agent, so a coding agent can deploy new LLMs on a spatial NPU autonomously.

family_reason: An LLM proposer edits the design each iteration from measured feedback work orders (diagnosed bottleneck, counters, history, prediction score) and a gate ladder, with a second LLM repairing failed gates.
scope_reason: The LLM edits Chisel RTL, memory configuration and a kernel schedule, and the outcome is hardware performance/energy/area of the accelerator design rather than the runtime efficiency of general software code.
gain_metric: cycles (cycle-accurate simulation, iteration 15 vs iteration 1)
baseline_name: Stock Gemmini running the block-sparse kernel (iteration 1)
gain_note: Table I (garbled row layout): cycles 106,650 -> 50,862; also off-chip bytes 3,211,264 -> 327,680, area 4.035 -> 3.115 mm2, modelled perf/W 10.96 -> 61.5 GOPS/W, EDP 20.41 -> 1.73 nJ.s. Single 15-iteration run on one workload with one model; no alternative LLM technique or ablation.
core_idea: A sealed Claude Code proposer inside the CHIA closed loop edits Gemmini Chisel RTL, memory parameters and sparse-kernel schedule via MCP tools, guided by measured-feedback work orders, and a gate ladder (legality, build, cycle-accurate simulation, bit-exact equivalence, synthesis) with an LLM repairer admits only Pareto-improving designs.
